stories.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: Team USA analysis, rankings, rosters
stories.summary: Sixteen nations will compete in the World Cup in Berlin starting Friday. Team USA and France are front-runners.
stories.body:
The WNBA season is paused for the next couple of weeks, but there's plenty of women's basketball being played. The 2026 FIBA World Cup begins Friday and will run through Sept. 13 in Berlin, Germany. The tournament might not be as prominent as the Olympics -- to fans, at least -- but it is one of two major international competitions, with this year's event featuring 16 teams from North America, Europe, Asia and Africa.

The United States is, per usual, stacked, though the reigning champions suffered a blow when it was announced Monday that four-time WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson and five-time All-Star Kelsey Plum are unable to participate in the tournament due to health reasons. But those losses don't alter the task at hand: bringing home a fifth consecutive World Cup gold and 12th overall.

The U.S. women's national team plays its group phase opener Friday against China. The USA faces Italy on Sunday and then Czechia on Monday. If the U.S. women win their group, they move on to the quarterfinals on Sept. 10, with the semifinals set for Sept. 12 and the championship and third-place games on Sept. 13.

There are plenty of other familiar faces in Berlin, too, with dozens of current and former WNBA players representing other countries, from Australia to Türkiye.

ESPN's World Cup guide gets you set with everything you need to know before the games tip. Not every roster has been finalized yet, but we list current WNBA players on each squad, along with their stats for this current WNBA season.

Jump to:

AUS | BEL | CHN | CZE | FRA | GER

HUN | ITA | JPN | KOR | MLI | NGR

PUR | ESP | TUR | USA | GROUPS

1. United States
Current WNBA players:

F/C Aliyah Boston, Indiana Fever (16.9 PPG, 8.3 RPG, 1.3 BPG)

G Paige Bueckers, Dallas Wings (20.5 PPG, 5.9 APG, 4.1 RPG)

G Sonia Citron, Washington Mystics (16.8 PPG, 4.3 APG, 1.2 SPG)

G Caitlin Clark, Indiana Fever (22.5 PPG, 8.4 APG, 3.9 RPG)

F Napheesa Collier, Minnesota Lynx (18.0 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 1.4 SPG)

F/G Kahleah Copper, Phoenix Mercury (21.3 PPG, 3.6 RPG, 1.9 APG)

G Chelsea Gray, Las Vegas Aces (12.0 PPG, 6.8 APG, 1.4 SPG)

G Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream (18.3 PPG, 3.6 APG, 2.3 SPG)

F Kiki Iriafen, Washington Mystics (15.3 PPG, 9.4 RPG, 0.7 SPG)

F Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream (16.1 PPG, 12.4 RPG, 1.8 SPG)

F Breanna Stewart, New York Liberty (20.4 PPG, 8.1 RPG, 1.4 BPG)

G Jackie Young, Las Vegas Aces (18.9 PPG, 6.6 APG, 4.4 RPG)

Outlook: The U.S. women's national basketball team is home to one of the most dominant dynasties in all of sports, winning eight consecutive Olympic gold medals and four straight World Cups. The program has lost just one game at a major international competition since 1994 -- the semifinals of the 2006 World Championship (later renamed World Cup) against Russia, where the Americans won bronze. Team USA has since won 30 consecutive World Cup games.

That is the legacy newly minted national team director Sue Bird, senior national team coach Kara Lawson and this young U.S. squad -- a group with seven players under 27 -- bring to Berlin. Fans have long anticipated seeing the likes of Clark, Bueckers and Reese compete against international competition as part of the senior national team. They got a taste of that at the World Cup qualifying tournament, where the USA went 5-0 and won by an average margin of 42 points.

But between the grueling schedule, heighted competition and pressure of representing the USA, the World Cup will be a much greater challenge. USA Basketball's youth movement will be tested even more so with Wilson, the reigning World Cup and Olympics MVP, and Plum no longer available. But they still have a core of experienced veterans in Stewart, Gray, Collier, Young and Copper, who know what it takes to win gold. -- Alexa Philippou

2. France
Current WNBA players:

G Pauline Astier, New York Liberty (9.2 PPG, 2.5 RPG, 3.4 APG)

F Valeriane Ayayi, Phoenix Mercury (6.3 PPG, 2.7 RPG, 1.3 APG)

G Marine Johannes, New York Liberty (8.5 PPG, 2.1 RPG, 2.4 APG)

G Leila Lacan, Connecticut Sun (11.6 PPG, 1.9 RPG, 4.6 APG)

G Carla Leite, Portland Fire (15.9 PPG, 2.1 RPG, 6.3 APG)

C Dominique Malonga, Seattle Storm (17.0 PPG, 9.0 RPG, 1.5 BPG)

F Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries (12.9 PPG, 3.9 RPG, 1.2 APG)

G Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries (14.3 PPG, 3.3 RPG, 2.2 APG)

Other notable players: C Marieme Badiane

Outlook: France, seen as the top threat to Team USA, might have its most talented roster ever with eight active WNBA players, four of whom will be headed to the playoffs. France has been building as an international power for the last several years. The French nearly toppled Team USA in the Olympic final in Paris in 2024, falling 67-66 behind former UConn star Williams' 19 points. France also took Olympic silver in 2012 and bronze in 2021.

France's only medal in the World Cup was a bronze in 1953, the first year of the event, but they are expected to have a podium finish this year. Malonga, the 2025 No. 2 WNBA draft pick who dunked in the All-Star Game in July, might look to do that in the World Cup. -- Michael Voepel

3. Spain

Current WNBA players:

G Elena Buenavida, Minnesota Lynx (developmental player)

C Raquel Carrera, New York Liberty (1.4 PPG, 1.1 RPG, 0.3 APG)

F Maria Conde, Toronto Tempo (8.9 PPG, 4.6 RPG, 2.6 APG)

C Megan DiLeo, Portland Fire (13.2 PPG, 4.2 RPG, 0.6 BPG)

C Awa Fam, Seattle Storm (10.3 PPG, 5.7 RPG, 0.9 SPG)

G Alicia Florez, Washington Mystics (3.3 PPG, 2.0 APG, 0.6 SPG)

Other notable players: G Iyana Martin, G Maite Cazorla

Outlook: Spain has had a relatively quiet output on the international stage in recent years. They medaled at the World Cup in 2010, 2014 and 2018 and took silver at the 2016 Olympics -- but then didn't even qualify for the previous World Cup in 2022 or the podium in Paris.

Coming off a silver-medal finish at last year's EuroBasket -- and more recently giving the USA its closest game of March's qualifying tournament -- Spain could be poised for a big showing in Berlin. The team is led by veteran Alba Torrens, the only player with World Cup experience, and has a naturalized star in DiLeo, who was a top-five scorer at the 2024 Olympics. Carrera has seen limited time with the Liberty but has been much more productive with her national team. What might be most anticipated, though, is the emergence of Spain's young tandem of 20-year-old stars in Storm rookie Fam and Martin, the Fire's draft-and-stash first-round selection. -- Philippou

4. Belgium

Current WNBA players:

G Julie Allemand, Toronto Tempo (6.3 PPG, 3.1 RPG, 5.6 APG)

C Kyara Linskens, Phoenix Mercury (3.0 PPG, 2.4 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

F Antonia Delaere, Minnesota Lynx (2.9 PPG, 0.7 RPG, 1.1 APG)

Other notable players: F Emma Meesseman, G Julie Vanloo, F Bethy Mununga

Outlook: Belgium should be one of the powers of Group C, along with Australia. The Cats are coached by longtime former WNBA coach Mike Thibault, who won a title with the Washington Mystics in 2019 when Meesseman was WNBA Finals MVP. Meesseman has played nine seasons in the WNBA, most recently last year when she spent 20 games (including the playoffs) with the New York Liberty. Vanloo played briefly (five games) with the Liberty this season. This is Allemand's fourth season in the WNBA, and she has been a starter for the expansion Tempo. This is Belgium's third World Cup appearance; they finished fourth in 2018 and fifth in 2022. Belgium has not medaled at the Olympics but had its best finish in Paris in 2024, falling in the bronze medal game. -- Voepel

5. Germany

Projected WNBA players:

F Frieda Buhner, Portland Fire (6.3 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 0.7 APG)

G Leonie Fiebich, New York Liberty (10.2 PPG, 3.0 RPG, 1.1 SPG)

C Luisa Geiselsoder, Portland Fire (4.5 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.3 APG)

F Nyara Sabally, Toronto Tempo (12.3 PPG, 5.3 RPG, 0.9 BPG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Just like in the Olympics, a World Cup host faces a mixture of pressure and opportunity, and it's no different for Germany in what is just its second time participating in the event (and first since 1998). Unfortunately the Germans will be without the services of star Satou Sabally, who has stepped away from basketball while recovering from the effects of her second concussion in eight months, and it's unclear how healthy her sister, Nyara, will be. For the Germans to earn their first podium finish at a major international competition, they will need a huge tournament from Fiebich, who has been showcasing her value with the Liberty upon returning from injury. But also expect the likes of Buhner and Geiselsoder to play even bigger roles than they do stateside in Portland. Germany is coached by Olaf Lange, current Tempo associate head coach and Sandy Brondello's husband. -- Philippou

6. China

Projected WNBA players:

C Han Xu, New York Liberty (6.4 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

* Roster is not yet finalized

Outlook: China should be the toughest challenger to Team USA in Group D, and the two play in the event opener for both. But the team was dealt a blow Wednesday when 6-foot-7 Dallas Wings center Li Yueru said on social media she will not be competing in Berlin because her passport was lost in the mail.

The United States and China faced off twice at the 2022 World Cup, with the U.S. women winning by 14 in group play and by 22 in the gold medal match. That result was still a win for the Chinese, though, as it marked the first time since 1994 that they earned a medal at a major international competition (both were silvers).

China faltered at the 2024 Olympics, finishing in ninth, before punching its ticket to the World Cup at this spring's qualifying tournament in Wuhan. This roster has some new faces compared to that '22 squad, headlined by the 7-foot-2, 19-year-old Zhang Ziyu. But she's not the only player who could pose some trouble for the USA, as the more experienced Han Xu (6-11) brings additional height. -- Philippou

7. Australia

Current WNBA players:

F Chloe Bibby, Minnesota Lynx (2.3 PPG, 0.7 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

G Isobel Borlase, Atlanta Dream (4.6 PPG, 1.5 RPG, 1.0 APG)

C Ezi Magbegor, Seattle Storm (6.9 PPG, 4.0 RPG, 1.2 BPG)

G Jade Melbourne, Seattle Storm (9.5 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 3.9 APG)

F Alanna Smith, Dallas Wings (6.0 PPG, 3.9 RPG, 1.0 APG)

G Miela Sowah, Golden State Valkyries (0.3 PPG, 0.8 RPG)

F Stephanie Talbot, Las Vegas Aces (3.5 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.0 APG)

Other notable players: F Alex Fowler, G Alex Wilson

Outlook: Phoenix Mercury guard Sami Whitcomb, captain of the Australian team, had to withdraw from the World Cup last week because of an ongoing knee injury. It's a big blow to the Opals regarding leadership and scoring. And it's heartbreaking for Whitcomb, who is 38. She was replaced by Sowah, 26. Sandy Brondello, who won WNBA titles with the Mercury (2014) and New York Liberty (2024) and is now with the Toronto Tempo, is Australia's coach.

The Opals began to emerge as an international power in women's basketball in the 1980s and won their first World Cup medal with a bronze in 1998. Their highlight was 2006, when they defeated Russia for the gold medal after the Russians had upset the United States in the semifinals. They also won bronze in 2002, 2014 and 2022, and took silver in 2018. Australia's six total World Cup medals puts them third on the all-time medal chart. The Aussies also have six Olympic medals: three silvers and three bronzes. -- Voepel

8. Italy

Current WNBA players:

G Costanza Verona, Dallas Wings (developmental player)

F Cecilia Zandalasini, Golden State Valkyries (8.8 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 1.8 APG)

Other notable players: F Lorela Cubaj

Outlook: Italy is enjoying a resurgence on the FIBA stage: Last year the team won its first EuroBasket medal since 1995 by beating France for the bronze medal, and now this World Cup marks the country's first appearance at a major international competition since the 1996 Olympics. Led by Zandalasini, the Italians lost 93-59 to the United States at the qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico, but went 4-1 overall at the event, including upsetting Spain the day after playing the U.S. women (and it's largely the same squad Italy has in Berlin). Italy has a difficult path ahead, though, having to face both the USA and China, the 2022 World Cup silver medalist, in the group phase. -- Philippou

9. Nigeria

Projected WNBA players:

F Amy Okonkwo, Portland Fire (4.3 PPG, 1.0 RPG, 0.3 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: This is the fourth time Nigeria has qualified for the World Cup, although it withdrew in 2022. That was much to the chagrin of the Nigerian players and FIBA. It was a decision by the Nigerian government, which opted in May 2022 to withdraw all its basketball teams from international competition while it restructured the sport's governance. Nigeria earned its World Cup berth this time by winning the AfroBasket 2025 championship. The team still played in the World Cup qualifying tournament in France in March, but lost three of five games. Nigeria's best finish in the World Cup is eighth, in 2018. The team's best Olympic finish is also eighth, in 2024. -- Voepel

10. Japan

Current WNBA players:

G Mai Yamamoto, Las Vegas Aces (5.8 PPG, 1.8 APG, 0.8 SPG)

Other notable players: G Rui Machida, G Kokoro Tanaka, C Ramu Tokashiki

Outlook: American basketball fans have come to enjoy Japan's entertaining style of play in recent years, particularly since squaring off against the USA in the 2020 Olympic gold medal game. Japan is known for speed, movement and 3-point shooting, which means the team can beat anyone if it gets hot -- and can lose to anyone if it can't hit shots. Lack of size is often an Achilles' heel -- just one player, Tokashiki, is listed over 6-foot.

Still, look out for the likes of Yamamoto, a midseason addition to the Aces, as well as Golden State draft pick Tanaka to make a splash on the perimeter. After the high of clinching silver at the Tokyo Olympics, Japan finished ninth at the 2022 World Cup, 12th at the Paris Olympics and almost didn't qualify for Berlin. Corey Gaines, the coach of the 2009 Phoenix Mercury championship squad, took over as head coach in early 2025. The pressure is on for them to find their form going into 2030, when they will host the next World Cup. -- Philippou

11. Hungary

Projected WNBA players:

F Dorka Juhász, Minnesota Lynx (3.8 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.2 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: While France is a big favorite in Group B, Hungary might make some waves behind Juhász. That especially could be the case with JiSu Park out for Korea and Nigeria looking kind of inconsistent entering the tournament. Hungary is making its sixth appearance in the World Cup but first since 1998. The team's best finish was fifth in 1957. -- Voepel

12. Korea

Current WNBA players:

G Jihyun Park, Los Angeles Sparks (2.2 PPG, 1.0 RPG, 0.5 APG)

Outlook: Korea is typically known as a strong outside shooting team. The team will need to rely even more on its guards with center JiSu Park, who played three seasons with the Las Vegas Aces, out due to an ankle injury. Korea is making its 18th World Cup appearance; it has played in every tournament except the first two in 1953 and 1957. Korea has won two silver medals, in 1967 and 1979. The team also has finished fourth three times, most recently in 2002. Korea has one medal in Olympic play, a silver in 1984. -- Voepel

13. Türkiye

Projected WNBA players:

G/F Kennedy Burke, Connecticut Sun (8.8 PPG, 3.2 RPG, 1.4 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Türkiye will learn a lot about its chances from its opener vs. Belgium. This is Türkiye's third appearance in the World Cup; the team was fourth in 2014, when it hosted the event, and 10th in 2018. In her seventh year in the WNBA, Burke is having a career-best season. -- Voepel

14. Mali

Projected WNBA players:

G Aicha Coulibaly, Chicago Sky (4.8 PPG, 2.8 RPG, 0.7 SPG)

F Sika Kone, Atlanta Dream (1.7 PPG, 1.0 RPG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Mali will make its third World Cup appearance, where it hopes to improve on an 11th-place finish in 2022. The program established itself as the second-best team out of Africa behind Nigeria, which beat Mali in the 2025 AfroBasket final. But Mali followed that up with a promising showing during the qualifying tournament in March, beating Czechia and narrowly losing to Brazil to clinch a spot in Berlin. Maimouna Haidara was the team's leading scorer in Wuhan, followed by the Dream's Kone; they'll need those two to dazzle to cause some upsets in Group A. -- Philippou

15. Czechia

Current WNBA players:

G Eliska Joklova, Minnesota Lynx (1.7 PPG, 1.1 APG, 1.0 RPG)

Outlook: Czechia is back at the World Cup after last appearing in the event in 2014; in 2010, it was the host nation and earned silver. The team's return this year has already been met with some concern. Czechia eked into the World Cup after a tepid qualifying tournament and has had some bad injury luck to two key players: Emma Cechova tore her ACL three games into her season with the Minnesota Lynx after a promising start, while Julia Reisingerova is also unavailable due to injury. On top of that, Czechia has to face the United States, China and a surging Italy squad in group play. It'll need sensational outings from the likes of Lynx rookie Joklova (née Hamzova), Veronika Vorackova and Petra Holesinska to keep up. -- Philippou

16. Puerto Rico

Current WNBA players: None

Other notable players: G Arella Guirantes, C Imani McGee-Stafford

Outlook: Host Puerto Rico was fourth in the qualifying tournament won by the United States in March in San Juan. A tough group awaits in Berlin, especially having to face Australia and Belgium. This is Puerto Rico's third appearance in the World Cup, having finished 16th in 2018 and eighth in 2022. Guirantes played two seasons in the WNBA, most recently in 2023. McGee-Stafford played four seasons in the league, most recently in 2019. Puerto Rico has competed twice in the Olympics. -- Voepel

Groups

Sixteen teams will compete in the FIBA World Cup in Berlin, Germany, with 36 games being played over 10 days from Sept. 4 to Sept. 13. The first-place team in each group advances to the quarterfinals; the second- and third-place teams will qualify for a single-game elimination format to determine the rest of the quarterfinalists.

stories.headline: NBA offseason recap, early 2026-27 season previews by team
stories.summary: We're looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the regular season by rolling out one team profile each weekday through Sept. 18.
stories.body:
After an eventful July full of big trades, intriguing signings and the game's biggest star shocking everyone by heading East, the NBA offseason is nearly complete. And with the regular-season schedule now out, it's time to start thinking about the 2026-27 season.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for every team.

Check out the rollout schedule below, with stories added daily:

Quick links:

Free agency buzz | FA grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Schedule | More NBA coverage

Southeast Division

Miami Heat: Aug. 31
Key additions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Nick Richards

Key retentions: Andrew Wiggins, Simone Fontecchio

Key subtractions: Tyler Herro, Norman Powell, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis

Heat president Pat Riley landed the superstar he'd been searching for since LeBron James left Miami in 2016. Antetokounmpo is in the fold, and Miami is ready to contend for another title with the two-time MVP. Antetokounmpo is just as motivated to win his second title and remind everyone that he can be the best player in the league.

In the trade, the Heat gave up key players such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez and did not bring back Powell in free agency. They landed Thompson to a two-year, $13 million deal after the four-time champion sharpshooter worked out a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks. Miami also added Portis and Hardaway, but the team is still looking to bolster the roster around Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Heat offseason recap/season preview

Washington Wizards: Sept. 1
Key additions: AJ Dybantsa, Khris Middleton, Deandre Ayton, Tre Mann

Key subtractions: Cam Whitmore, D'Angelo Russell, Jaden Hardy

Key retentions: Trae Young

The Wizards got their jump on this pivotal offseason by acquiring Trae Young and Anthony Davis last season in trades.

Those were their two big moves and then came the big prize for losing 65 games last season - winning the lottery and drafting AJ Dybantsa with the first overall pick.

Ready to start winning games this season after losing 60 or more games in each of the past three years, Washington gave Young a four-year, $212 million contract. The Wizards added veterans like Khris Middleton and Deandre Ayton to bolster the depth behind their young core featuring the likes of Dybantsa, Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George, Tre Johnson and Will Riley. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Wizards offseason recap/season preview

Charlotte Hornets: Sept. 2
Key additions: F Naz Reid, G Grayson Allen, G Dennis Schroder, F Royce O'Neale, F Dorian Finney-Smith

Key retentions: G Coby White

Key subtractions: G LaMelo Ball, F Miles Bridges, G Josh Green, G Tre Mann

After enjoying their best season in a decade, the Hornets sharply changed course with the surprising decision to trade Ball, their franchise guard, to the Timberwolves.

Given that Ball was a borderline All-Star on a max contract, Charlotte opted for a "Moneyball" approach in hopes of avoiding the perpetual mediocrity that tripped up Trae Young's Atlanta Hawks in the recent past.

With Ball and starting forward Miles Bridges moved in separate deals aimed at collecting future draft assets and improving its cap flexibility, Charlotte is now the only team that doesn't have a single player on the books for at least $25 million next season. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Hornets offseason recap/season preview

Atlanta Hawks: Sept. 3
Key additions: Luguentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins, Kingston Flemings, Devin Carter, Ryan Nembhard, Zuby Ejiofor, Henri Veesaar

Key retentions: CJ McCollum, Jock Landale

Key subtractions: Zaccharie Risacher, Jonathan Kuminga, Gabe Vincent, Keaton Wallace

Atlanta continued to move forward from the Trae Young trade last season by being opportunistic this offseason.

The Hawks acquired Dort and Wiggins in separate trades from the Oklahoma City Thunder to add more help around emerging star Jalen Johnson. The Hawks also kept McCollum on a one-year, $21 million deal and drafted Flemings eighth overall.

Atlanta is loaded with young wings looking to take a step forward under Quin Snyder like Nickeil Alexander-Walker did last season in winning Most Improved Player. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Read the full Hawks offseason recap/season preview

Orlando Magic: Sept. 4

Pacific Division

Los Angeles Lakers: Aug. 24
Key additions: C Walker Kessler, F Sandro Mamukelashvili, G Quentin Grimes, G Collin Sexton, F Kevon Looney, F Matisse Thybulle, G Cameron Carr

Key retentions: G Austin Reaves

Key subtractions: F LeBron James, C Deandre Ayton, G Marcus Smart, F Rui Hachimura, G Luke Kennard, C Jaxson Hayes

James informed the Lakers he would not be returning for next season on June 30. Two days later, the team transformed the roster, with Doncic squarely as the focal point.

The biggest addition -- literally and figuratively -- is 7-foot-2 center Kessler, acquired in a sign-and-trade deal with the Utah Jazz. L.A. sent two unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and pick swaps in 2028 and 2030, not to mention a four-year, $130 million contract, to acquire him.

Mamukelashvili, Grimes, Sexton, Looney and Thybulle also signed with the Lakers, and free agent Ziaire Williams and first-round pick Carr bolster the team's young prospect pool of Adou Thiero, Bronny James and Dalton Knecht.

The most important move, though, came when Reaves, coming off a career season in which he averaged 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game, signed a four-year, $180 million extension.

When the dust settled, it was a dramatic roster overhaul in what could prove to be one of the most consequential summers in franchise history, with the team also being sold for the second time in 14 months, this time to venture capitalist Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger, who bought the Lakers from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Lakers offseason recap/season preview

LA Clippers: Aug. 25
Key additions: Rui Hachimura, Keaton Wagler, Brandon Ingram (TBD), Gradey Dick (TBD)

Key retentions: Kobe Sanders, Bradley Beal

Key subtractions: Kawhi Leonard (TBD), Nicolas Batum, Bogdan Bogdanovic, John Collins

What started as a reconfiguration at the trade deadline -- acquiring Darius Garland from Cleveland for James Harden and Bennedict Mathurin from Indiana for Ivica Zubac -- turned into a complete overhaul this summer after the Clippers let Bogdan Bogdanovic, Nicolas Batum and John Collins walk.

Their biggest move, however, was trading Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and draft picks, but that deal is in limbo pending the investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention by the team relating to Leonard's Aspiration endorsement deal.

In the meantime, LA added Illinois guard Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the draft and signed Hachimura away from the crosstown Lakers with a two-year, $28 million deal. And in a surprise move, Bradley Beal -- after declining his $5.6 million contract option for next season in June to test free agency -- ended up re-signing on a two-year, $13.2 million deal in mid-August to stay with the Clippers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Clippers offseason recap/season preview

Golden State Warriors: Aug. 26
Key additions: Yaxel Lendeborg, Brandon Williams, Georges Niang

Key subtractions: Quinten Post, Pat Spencer

Key retentions: Draymond Green, Al Horford, Kristaps Porzingis, Gary Payton II, De'Anthony Melton

The Warriors opted for flexibility and stability over a larger shake-up around Curry. Their much-publicized recruitment of James never gained much traction.

They brought back their veteran frontcourt trio (Green, Horford, Porzingis), but kept them all on short-term maneuverable contracts. They opted for the fit of Melton over a pursuit of scoring guard Anfernee Simons. Their big addition is Lendeborg, the 23-year-old rookie wing who they will rely upon to be a high-minute, high-impact rotation player immediately.

In the bigger picture, they protected their draft pick cupboard and lined up their books to have an ocean of cap space as they peer a bit deeper into the future while their core ages. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Warriors offseason recap/season preview

Phoenix Suns: Aug. 27
Key additions: F Miles Bridges, F Koa Peat, G Luke Kennard

Key subtractions: G Grayson Allen, F Royce O'Neale

Key retentions: F Dillon Brooks, G Collin Gillespie, C Mark Williams, G Jordan Goodwin

Phoenix followed up its surprising season with a series of moves to mostly keep its team intact, with some adjustments around the margins.

The Suns re-signed Gillespie (four years, $48 million), Williams (three years, $38 million), Goodwin (three years, $19 million) and Brooks (three years, $73 million) to new deals and made a major splash by trading Allen and O'Neale to the Charlotte Hornets for Bridges. And despite not having a pick until No. 47 in the second round of the 2026 draft, Phoenix was able to acquire Arizona player Peat -- who averaged 14.1 points on 52.8% shooting as a freshman for the Wildcats and was key to their Final Four run. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Suns offseason recap/season preview

Sacramento Kings: Aug. 28
Key additions: G Darius Acuff Jr., F Alex Karaban, G Emanuel Sharp

Key subtractions: G DeMar DeRozan, G Russell Westbrook

Key retentions: F Precious Achiuwa

Perry, currently in the organization's power seat, is continuing a steady transition toward the younger core he has drafted. Arkansas guard and No. 7 pick Acuff is the spotlight name on a roster populated with six players in their first two NBA seasons.

But they still have notable high-minute holdovers from the past regime, including Murray, Malik Monk, LaVine and Sabonis. Of those four, Murray appears the most locked-in as a stable member of the team's long-term vision. Perry explored trades for Monk, LaVine and Sabonis over the past year, but didn't value the proposed returns, and the three are expected to open the season in Sacramento. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Kings offseason recap/season preview

Northwest Division

Portland Trail Blazers: Aug. 17
Key additions: G Ja Morant, F Jeremy Sochan

Key retentions: C Robert Williams III

Key subtractions: F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, G Matisse Thybulle

Sadly, the Blazers made far more noise this offseason with their off-court business dealings than anything they did with their roster. New owner Tom Dundon's aggressive cost-cutting measures and ongoing fight for arena financing have distracted from the progress that Portland made on the court last season, when it reached the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

Although the Blazers were the only team that sat out June's draft by not making a pick, they will add two high-profile guards to a rotation that otherwise looks very similar to last season. Lillard, a franchise icon, is back from an Achilles tendon injury that sidelined him for the entire 2025-26 campaign, and Morant, a two-time All-Star, arrived in a trade that sent Grant and Murray to the Memphis Grizzlies. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Blazers offseason recap/season preview

Utah Jazz: Aug. 18
Key additions: G Darryn Peterson, C Jaxson Hayes, G Josh Okogie

Key retentions: C Jusuf Nurkic

Key subtractions: C Walker Kessler

The Jazz finally got some lottery luck, landing at No. 2 and taking Peterson, a gifted guard who has the potential to emerge as the face of the franchise. The hope was that Peterson would be the final major piece in Utah's rebuild, but that plan featured Kessler as the team's long-term starting center. Instead, the Jazz agreed to a sign-and-trade deal that sent Kessler to the Lakers in exchange for a pair of future first-round picks and two swaps.

The return was widely considered to be great value for Utah, particularly after Kessler's deal (four years, $130 million) pushed beyond the Jazz's comfort zone, but there is now a glaring need in the starting lineup alongside Jackson and Lauri Markkanen in the frontcourt. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Jazz offseason recap/season preview

Minnesota Timberwolves: Aug. 19
Key additions: G LaMelo Ball, G Josh Green, G Isaiah Evans

Key subtractions: F Julius Randle, C Naz Reid

Key retentions: G Ayo Dosunmu, G Bones Hyland, G Jaylen Clark

Wolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly continued to show his aggression, orchestrating a four-team trade with the Brooklyn Nets, Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets that sent out three-time All-Star Randle and the 2023-24 Sixth Man of the Year, Reid, and a future first-round pick to bring in the talented -- but polarizing -- Ball.

That move followed Connelly inking 6-foot-4 guard Dosunmu to a five-year, $112 million extension in June, following his acquisition at the deadline.

Minnesota also re-signed wing Clark and guard Hyland and acquired the 6-foot-6 Evans out of Duke with the No. 33 pick in the draft.

Coach Chris Finch also lost his top lieutenant on the bench, Micah Nori, who left to coach the Portland Trail Blazers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Timberwolves offseason recap/season preview

Oklahoma City Thunder: Aug. 20
Key additions: C Aday Mara, G Bennett Stirtz

Key retentions: G Kenrich Williams, C Isaiah Hartenstein

Key subtractions: G Isaiah Joe, G Aaron Wiggins, G Luguentz Dort

The extensions for both Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren triggered in July, leading to a trio of financially motivated trades to slash the tax bill and cost-control the current roster.

They sent Isaiah Joe to Detroit and traded Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort to Atlanta in separate moves, eroding their depth.

General manager Sam Presti made clear in an interview with The Oklahoman that the impression he's been given from ownership is "the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be re-allocated to future teams."

That would mean extra breathing room to eventually extend core young players such as Cason Wallace and Ajay Mitchell. Wallace, the likely replacement starter for Dort, is extension eligible off his rookie contract into October. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Thunder offseason recap/season preview

Denver Nuggets: Aug. 21
Key additions: Marvin Bagley III, Lonnie Walker IV

Key retentions: Spencer Jones, Tyus Jones

Key subtractions: Watson, Tim Hardaway Jr., Jonas Valanciunas

Finding a resolution to Watson's restricted free agency was Denver's most important piece of summer business.

Watson is a draft success story, rising from the 30th overall pick into one of the league's more intriguing young two-way wings. But retaining the 23-year-old would have been expensive -- via either a sky-high luxury tax bill or a salary-slashing move to get off an important veteran and generate more breathing room for a new deal.

After Wednesday's deal to send Watson to Cleveland, Denver's front office can shift its attention to escaping the salary cap's second apron. The Nuggets are currently the league's only team above it. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Nuggets offseason recap/season preview

Southwest Division

Memphis Grizzlies: Aug. 14
Key additions: F Cameron Boozer, G D'Angelo Russell, F Isaiah Stewart, F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, C Quinten Post

Key retentions: None

Key subtractions: G Ja Morant, F Santi Aldama

Memphis finally traded Ja Morant, turning the last page from an ultimately disappointing chapter in franchise history, and already has his replacement as the face of the franchise in place: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer. GM Zach Kleiman has overhauled the roster in the past few transaction cycles, acquiring four first-round picks when he traded Desmond Bane, a few more when he dealt Jaren Jackson Jr. and none for Morant, whose departure signaled a fresh start for the Grizzlies and him.

Memphis is in a full-blown youth movement, as 21-year-old forward GG Jackson is now the longest-tenured player on the roster. The Grizzlies say they believe they have a long-term foundation in place with their last few lottery picks: center Zach Edey, small forward Cedric Coward and power forward Boozer. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Grizzlies offseason recap/season preview

New Orleans Pelicans: Aug. 13
Key additions: None

Key retentions: C DeAndre Jordan

Key subtractions: F Kevon Looney

Despite capturing a combined 47 wins over the last two seasons under executive vice president Joe Dumars and general manager Troy Weaver, the Pelicans clearly believe that internal growth is the best path forward. Perhaps that justifies a near-silent summer in which the hiring of new coach Jamahl Mosley turned out to be the team's most notable move. Mosley becomes New Orleans' third coach since Dumars took the helm in April 2025. In addition to drafting Jaron Pierre Jr. in the second round, New Orleans signed just two new players over the summer in Kobe Bufkin and Hunter Dickinson, while bringing back 14 of the 15 players from last season's squad. -- Michael C. Wright

Read the full Pelicans offseason recap/season preview

Dallas Mavericks: Aug. 12
Key additions: F Morez Johnson Jr., F Zaccharie Risacher

Key retentions: Moussa Cisse

Key subtractions: Khris Middleton, Ryan Nembhard

The major changes made by the Mavericks this offseason were in the managerial and coaching ranks. After a seasonlong search, team governor Patrick Dumont hired Masai Ujiri to run the franchise's basketball operations, bringing the architect of the Toronto Raptors' 2019 title team to Dallas. Ujiri decided to part ways with coach Jason Kidd and recruited Dusty May, fresh off an NCAA title with Michigan, to replace him.

Johnson, who played for May at Michigan before the Mavs selected him with the No. 9 pick in the draft, is the headliner of the additions to the roster. Dallas added three potential immediate contributors in a six-team deal, acquiring former Grizzlies forward Santi Aldama, ex-Pistons guard Marcus Sasser and EuroLeague veteran Tarik Biberovic. The franchise also landed former No. 1 pick as part of the trade that sent Luguentz Dort from the Oklahoma City Thunder to the Atlanta Hawks. -- MacMahon

Read the full Mavericks offseason recap/season preview

Houston Rockets: Aug. 11
Key additions: G Marcus Smart, G Bogdan Bogdanovic

Key retentions: F Tari Eason

Key subtractions: F Dorian Finney-Smith, G Josh Okogie

After suffering a first-round postseason exit for the second consecutive season, the Rockets resisted the temptation to jump into the Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes after adding former MVP Durant last summer. General manager Rafael Stone and coach Ime Udoka will instead lean on growth from the team's collection of young talent acquired in recent years, not to mention the continuity that comes with those players developing together over multiple seasons.

Houston signed Tari Eason to a five-year, $81.5 million extension over the summer. But outside of that, the Rockets focused on bolstering depth by bringing aboard veterans Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic. The club also brought in renowned shooting coach Chip Engelland from Oklahoma City. Engelland spent more than a decade with the San Antonio Spurs, winning two titles. -- Wright

Read the full Rockets offseason recap/season preview

San Antonio Spurs: Aug. 10
Key additions: F Tobias Harris

Key retentions: F Harrison Barnes

Key subtractions: None

San Antonio's surprising run to the NBA Finals never obscured its long-term vision for building a sustainable competitor around Victor Wembanyama. Clearly, the Frenchman views the future similarly, considering he signed a 25% max extension worth $252 million instead of the available 30% supermax escalators that would've rocketed the contract to $303 million.

Wembanyama did it to keep San Antonio's talented young core together for as long as possible, with added flexibility to acquire needed supporting players. The Spurs grabbed one of those in free agency in Harris, an experienced, reliable scorer who adds size (6-foot-8, 226 pounds) and physicality on defense while bolstering frontcourt depth in the draft. -- Wright

stories.headline: Fantasy football fast facts: Quick-hit notes to get you ready for your draft
stories.summary: Forgot to do your fantasy football homework and need some facts on big names at the most important positions?
stories.body:
Welcome to Labor Day weekend, the busiest time on the fantasy football draft calendar. Don't challenge me, as I have the power of ESPN Research to back that up! Some of you might not have put in your homework because it seemed so far away (kind of like your humanities course in college). But now it's final exam time, and you didn't study. And yes, I still have that same recurring dream.

I know, there is so much more we could talk about, but I wanted to give you the CliffsNotes to get you started for a great draft weekend. And one last thing, if you play in a fantasy league with somebody who provides fantasy analysis for a living -- maybe ask him or her if there was any breaking news before the draft. I know that seems hyper specific, and it's meant to be because my friend didn't do that last weekend. But still, just do a quick news search while you're hitting the charcuterie board before the draft. (Also not to brag, but I spelled charcuterie correctly on the first try. My first win of the season.)

Here are some fast facts (and a little opinion) to help you get through your draft prep.

Jump ahead

Quarterback notes | Running back notes

Wide receiver notes | Tight end notes

Quarterback notes

• Malik Willis is the modern-day Matt Flynn (Google him, kids), turning one great start into a lucrative free agent contract with the Miami Dolphins. But the reason you should like Willis is his rushing ability. He had 60 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns in his lone start for the Green Bay Packers in 2025 -- which was about 60 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns more than Matthew Stafford. And don't worry, it doesn't seem like there is a Russell Wilson there to take Willis' gig. Again, Google these references. It was a wild time.

• Drake Maye was sacked a career-high 68 times in 2025, including the playoffs. Even with offensive line help from first-round pick Caleb Lomu and free agency signing Alijah Vera-Tucker, I'm not saying you avoid Maye altogether. He's really good, and the New England Patriots went out and got A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. But I've seen him fly off the board as high as QB2 ahead of Joe Burrow for instance. Do what you want, but I love other options such as Justin Herbert or Trevor Lawrence, who have much better value later in drafts.

• Aaron Rodgers ranked last in air yards per attempt (6.0) in 2025. Michael Pittman Jr. ranked 68th in average depth of target last year. Sounds like a great match. For Pittman, I wouldn't touch Rodgers this season. Maybe he can recapture the magic with Mike McCarthy, but this looks like one of those reboots they should have never attempted.

• Patrick Mahomes tore his left ACL/LCL in Week 15. He's expected to start Week 1 against the Denver Broncos. It's strange that his ADP puts him as a QB2. I mean, I don't normally draft two quarterbacks but would be willing to make an exception here.

• Everyone loves CeeDee Lamb. They love George Pickens. What will it take for Dak Prescott to get the love from fantasy managers? He's going to outplay his ADP this year. He is currently the QB7 on ESPN, although anecdotally, I've seen him drop much further. Dak had 30 passing touchdowns last season, but I'm projecting him closer to 40 this year, which would land him closer to the top three.

• I want to believe Geno Smith will be great for Garrett Wilson. But Smith was one of the worst quarterbacks in terms of air yards per completion (4.3), down there with Bo Nix (4.8), Bryce Young (4.8) and Tua Tagovailoa (4.7). You could reason Wilson gives him a chance to improve that number. But are you willing to risk drafting Wilson in the hope that Smith gets better?

• Baker Mayfield had a 16-2 TD-INT ratio from Weeks 1 through 10. It was 10-9 from Weeks 11 through 19. Now if you want to go with narratives, a motivated Mayfield going for a new contract could regain that form. Or without Mike Evans, he could be what he was at the end of the season. If WR Emeka Egbuka performs like he did in the first half of the season, that could be a big help to Mayfield. Ebuka averaged 89 yards and scored five touchdowns in the first five weeks of the season.

• Jared Goff has led the NFL in passing yards per game (270), games with 300-plus passing yards (17) and passing touchdowns (101). He's not being drafted as a QB1. Is it the lack of running? Because it's something that goes against Stafford, too. Make sure you check your league's scoring settings, however. Because a quarterback such as Goff (and Stafford) are much more valuable in leagues where you get six points for a passing touchdown.

• The Philadelphia Eagles lost five of their last eight games. People are fading Jalen Hurts. Anybody think part of the problem could have been the injury to Lane Johnson? Hurts could be due for a huge bounce back as the former All-Pro tackle goes on his retirement tour. You're getting Hurts at a discount.

Running back notes
This is a good time to bring this up as we get into non-QBs: Please check your league rules before the draft. Do you start three receivers or two? Do you have one flex spot or two? This will impact your decisions.

I should also tell you, make sure you get your RB2 before you exit the fourth round. That might even be too late. We've gone from Zero RB to Hero RB to fear o' RB if you try to get too cute.

• Christian McCaffrey has fallen off severely every time he has had 400 touches in a season. Guess what? He had more than 400 touches last year. It would be wise to stay away, like my guy Daniel Dopp has advocated, but I can't stay away from the thought that he's going to end up being the 49ers most-targeted pass catcher this season. George Kittle is working toward being available for the 49ers, while his teammate De'Zhaun Stribling is another player fantasy managers are looking at. But in this sense, I'm taking the known quantity and rolling with McCaffrey. Even if this might end up costing me.

• Kenneth Walker III is the No.1 guy for the Kansas City Chiefs, which opens the door for Jadarian Price in Seattle. His ADP has risen over the summer for good reason. He's going to be the guy before Zach Charbonnet returns from the PUP list that will force him to miss at least four games.

• Derrick Henry is the only player in NFL history with 1,500-plus rushing yards and 15-plus rushing touchdowns in a season at age 30 or older. Are you ready to run it back? Field Yates says so. I'm kind of into it as well.

• Chase Brown is one of four players with 2,000-plus rushing yards and 750-plus receiving yards since 2024. The others? Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson and De'Von Achane. So yeah, not bad company!

• Speaking of De'Von Achane, I can talk myself into him being a huge risk because the Dolphins are going to be miserable. But I can also talk myself into him being a great value because there is nobody else to trust. And then I can see Bobby Slowik as offensive coordinator and instantly regret taking Achane at his ADP (right at the end of the first round).

• You need to put more respect on James Cook III. Maybe not you, but your friends who are letting him slide until late in the first. The Bills have run on 49.3% of offensive plays since 2024 (fourth highest in the NFL). The Bills led the NFL with 32.2 carries with 159.7 rushing yards per game in 2025.

• David Montgomery has 33 rushing touchdowns since 2023 (sixth-highest total for a running back over that stretch). The Texans have had 34 rushing touchdowns since that time.

• Travis Etienne Jr. led the Jacksonville Jaguars with 1,399 scrimmage yards and a 13-high scrimmage touchdowns in 2025. He's with the New Orleans Saints now. Bhayshul Tuten is expected to be the RB1 on a team that had 22 rushing touchdowns last season. I would even project the Jaguars to run the ball a bit more this season. The Jaguars' first pick in the 2026 NFL draft was TE Nate Boerkircher out of Texas A&M, which many saw as a reach. I saw this as an opportunity for the Jaguars to strengthen their rushing attack with multiple tight end sets.

• RJ Harvey was eighth among NFL running backs with 47 receptions. His five receiving touchdowns for the Denver Broncos were the second-highest total in the league behind only CMC.

• MarShawn Lloyd is seeing his ADP rise after the Josh Jacobs news. But Kaleb Johnson is getting a second chance with the team. I'm intrigued as a flyer in deeper leagues. What I'm trying to tell you is don't break the bank trying to get Jacobs' replacement.

• I know it's easy to say Omarion Hampton will be the Achane of the Los Angeles Chargers with new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel -- so that's exactly what I will do. I would take Hampton over Henry or Saquon Barkley.

• We love Cam Skattebo for the reasons we, well, love Cam Skattebo. But he's so much more! Like when you liked Mick Foley for jumping off cages, but you don't realize he was a better wrestler than you gave him credit for. Did you know Skattebo had the second-most receptions for the Giants (24) from Weeks 1 through 8?

Wide receiver notes

• You might be excited about Carnell Tate this season, and I don't want to talk you out of that. But remember Wan'Dale Robinson signed a huge deal with the Titans. Robinson -- who played for new offensive coordinator Brian Daboll -- had 185 receptions from 2024-25, the seventh most in the NFL over that span.

• I know we didn't trust Quentin Johnston before because he had trouble with drops in 2024 (seven of them, to be exact). But he was much better with the drops last season and had eight touchdowns. Could McDaniel unlock him in 2026?

• Are we sleeping on Tre Tucker, who led the Raiders with 696 receiving yards last season? Yeah, probably. Break the bank for Brock Bowers. The Raiders have Bowers as the top pass catcher. I had been counting on Ashton Jeanty to step it up in this area. But who else can the Raiders rely on? I know, I'm supposed to answer that question. It's going to be Mike Washington Jr. He did have 28 receptions at Arkansas, where he averaged 8.1 yards per reception. The Raiders could use him as a receiver out of the backfield to help with the receiver deficiencies.

• The Broncos are turning playcalling over to Davis Webb this season. That could be huge for new receiver Jaylen Waddle. Webb joked with reporters that Waddle will line up everywhere but on the offensive line. He even compared Waddle coming to Denver like Stefon Diggs going to Buffalo. We're going a little crazy with comparisons, and I don't want to do the whole "Waddle can be 2019 Michael Thomas for the Broncos" thing ... but I'm going to.

• Tetairoa McMillan had 30.7% of his team's receiving yards last season. Not quite where Puka Nacua was during his rookie season (34.6), but more than Ja'Marr Chase (30.3).

Tight end notes

• The Bears have loaded up on offensive firepower, which is great for Caleb Williams. But it might drive you crazy trying to figure out who emerges from Luther Burden III, Rome Odunze, D'Andre Swift, etc. I'd lock in on Colston Loveland, who had a massive 48 targets over his last four games (including the playoffs). Plus, Williams had a completion percentage of 74.3 when targeting Burden and Loveland. It was 52.8 for everyone else.

• Kyle Pitts Sr. signed an extension in 2026. He had 928 receiving yards last year, the most since his rookie season, and tight ends have thrived under Kevin Stefanski. I'm ready to be hurt again by going after Pitts.

• Trey McBride had 63 receptions for 644 yards and six receiving touchdowns while lined up in the slot last year, the highest in the NFL. What this means is that you're basically drafting a slot receiver (and the Cardinals top option) for a tight end designation.

• Terrance Ferguson is worth a flier if you miss out on all of the elite-level tight ends this year. New Fergie could end up being the de facto Rams WR3, but with a tight end designation.

• Michael Wilson (78 receptions for 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns) is the receiver you think Marvin Harrison Jr. is. But hey, I also can talk myself into drafting the former first-round pick.

stories.headline: Blues name Thomas as captain despite last season's trade rumors
stories.summary: The Blues have named center Robert Thomas as the 25th captain in franchise history just months after his name was heavily circulated in trade rumors.
stories.body:
The St. Louis Blues have named center Robert Thomas as the 25th captain in franchise history, months after his name was heavily circulated in trade rumors.

Thomas, 27, led the Blues with 64 points (25 goals, 39 assists) in 64 games last season, skating to a plus-22. Thomas has 132 goals and 328 assists in 530 career games. He's entering his ninth NHL season after being selected by St. Louis 20th overall in the 2017 NHL draft. Thomas will become the seventh original Blues draft pick to be named captain.

Thomas replaces Brayden Schenn as captain, who was traded to the New York Islanders at last season's deadline.

Defensemen Colton Parayko and Philip Broberg, and forwards Jake Neighbours and Dylan Holloway, will be named assistant captains for the 2026-27 season at a news conference Thursday.

Thomas is signed through the 2030-31 NHL season with an average annual contract value of $8.125 million. He has a full no-movement clause until the last year of his contract, but that didn't stop his name from whirling through the rumor mill last season. The Minnesota Wild and Buffalo Sabres were among the teams that made offers for Thomas, but those talks never reached the point where the Blues asked Thomas to waive his trade protection.

stories.headline: Why does the Italian GP trophy look like a pile of washing up?
stories.summary: The winner of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix will receive a trophy that looks like a pile of washing up after Pirelli commissioned two artists to come up with the design.
stories.body:
The winner of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix will receive a trophy that looks like a pile of washing up after Pirelli commissioned two artists to come up with the design.

For the past six years, Pirelli, the official sponsor of the Italian Grand Prix, has commissioned Italian artists to design the trophies presented to the top three drivers and winning constructor on Monza's famous podium.

This year the commission was awarded to Vedovamazzei, an art duo made up of Stella Scala and Simeone Crispino.

The trophy, named FRAGILE, is designed to look like a series of mugs and bowls precariously stacked on top of each other.

- Italian Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule

- Ferrari to run Schumacher tribute livery at Monza

- Hamilton takes ownership of Ferrari F40 road car

Why is the trophy designed this way?
"One day, while putting a bowl in the sink, we suddenly realised that the trophy was right there in front of us," the artists said. "The sink saved the aesthetics of the piece."

The trophy is produced from nylon polymer using a 3D printing process before being painted, galvanized, and polished until it becomes reflective.

"The idea for the trophy stems from the ancient tradition of passing a celebratory cup from hand to hand. It served as a large drinking vessel, creating a sense of shared celebration and festivity."

"We wanted the trophy to be the symbol of a victory that an individual holds in their hands, yet it reflects the spirit of a community," the artists added. "In the case of Formula 1, this community includes the team, the fans, and the entire world revolving around the drivers.

"The composition also evokes an everyday dimension with its repeated gestures, suggesting a victory earned lap after lap that never corresponds to an eternal, unchanging status. It is unstable, short-lived, and must be reclaimed. In fact, it is fragile."

stories.headline: Song Yadong KO's Umar Nurmagomedov in massive UFC upset
stories.summary: Song Yadong pulled off a massive upset by knocking out heavily favored Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night in Shanghai.
stories.body:
Song Yadong saved the greatest performance of his career for his home country, knocking out former title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night on Saturday in Shanghai.

Song (24-9-1, 1 NC), a nearly 5-1 underdog at DraftKings Sportsbook, dropped Nurmagomedov with a short right hand, drawing a roar from the crowd when the fight was waved off at 1 minute, 48 seconds of Round 2.

"I believe in myself, and my team believed that I would win this fight," Song said through an interpreter. "They told me I would knock this guy out, and I did it."

It was the second straight fight in China for Song and his second straight win by finish. His most recent knockout win had been in 2023.

Song, making his first appearance in Shanghai since his UFC debut at age 19 in 2017, walked out to a hero's welcome.

"Nine years ago, I wanted to show I could walk in this Octagon," he said. "Nine years later, I want to prove I am the best in the world. I am the best Chinese fighter in the world."

The knockout came after Nurmagomedov (20-2) ducked out of the way of a left hand and right into the path of a short right hand, which connected near his right ear and sent him limply to the canvas. Song delivered three finishing shots on the mat before the referee jumped in.

That sent Song running around inside the cage in celebration, where he nearly ran into Nurmagomedov's younger brother and cornerman, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, who had rushed in to check on his fallen brother. Usman Nurmagomedov appeared to throw an elbow in Song's direction as the elated winner was running past.

Song climbed atop the cage to soak in the fans' cheers before jumping down outside the cage and running into the crowd to get hugs and high-fives from fans.

"Maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, maybe not next month, but I will be the first male Chinese UFC champion," Song said through the interpreter, with the "male" designation a nod to countrywoman Zhang Weili, a two-time women's champion at strawweight.

Song, who trains in Sacramento, California, switched to English and yelled, "Give me the title shot!"

stories.headline: Roosters coach backs NRL wildcard weekend
stories.summary: Trent Robinson has defended his decision to rest nine players ahead of the NRL finals, but would be in favour of a wildcard weekend to fixture a break for the top teams.
stories.body:
Trent Robinson has defended his decision to rest nine players ahead of the NRL finals, but would be in favour of a wildcard weekend to fixture a break for the top teams.

The fourth-placed Sydney Roosters drifted to $7 outsiders after announcing they would rest James Tedesco, Daly Cherry-Evans and seven others from Friday's clash with South Sydney.

Following Sam Walker's injury, Robinson admitted there was a temptation to give new halves combination Cherry-Evans and Hugo Savala a dry run in the last weekend before finals.

"There was some thought around that, but I also trust the way that they both play," he said.

"They've both trained a lot together."

The upheaval on the Roosters' team sheet comes after Penrith memorably rested 16 players for the penultimate round of last season, while finals-bound Cronulla and the Warriors are also resting fit players this weekend.

The situation has reignited suggestions of introducing a pre-finals wildcard round.

That would allow the teams that finish between first and sixth to rest the weekend before finals and therefore play full strength until the end of the regular season.

The teams placed seventh to 10th, meanwhile, would play off to secure one of two finals spots, so would have incentive to name their best teams.

The AFL welcomed 172,769 fans to the two games across their first wildcard weekend last month.

It is understood NRL club chief executive officers were broadly in favour of introducing the concept when quizzed at Wednesday's meeting.

Robinson is also keen on introducing a wildcard weekend, but only once the league expands closer to 20 teams as it aims by the end of the decade.

"I think it makes commercial sense, I think it makes football sense as far as the weekend off and making the finals series at its best as well for those teams," he said.

"I think it's with some foresight not to (use it as we) go to 18 (teams), but probably going towards 20, and I think it's not all four of those teams getting into that finals series, it's only two of them.

"So you're not rewarding four teams, you're rewarding two teams that have to fight their way in."

Rex Bassingthwaighte, Toby Rodwell and Reece Foley all join the Roosters' starting backline with four NRL games of experience between them, while uncapped Hayden Barton, Aston Warwick and Jake Elliott are on the six-man bench.

Robinson insisted he was still taking the clash, between the NRL's two fiercest rivals, seriously.

"History will show that I love this game and respect this game, and I don't think there's any different this weekend, because Daly Cherry-Evans isn't playing and Toby Rodwell is," he said.

"There's a future in what we're going to be playing out there as well."

Rabbitohs coach Wayne Bennett shrugged at the Roosters' decision to rest players.

"I've done it before myself as a coach," he said.

"They know where they are in the competition and they're well placed, so it's not a bad time to give someone a rest if they need it."

Souths can secure a home final by defeating the Roosters and do not have a preference between hosting at Allianz or Accor Stadium.

Cronulla, meanwhile, are growing increasingly confident they will be able to host their home final at Shark Park despite its reduced capacity.

The Sharks are likely to finish fifth and face North Queensland, who are not expected to have a large enough contingent of travelling fans to warrant a bigger venue.
